profiles.meeting_scenario: A troubleshooting meeting at a market surveillance technology vendor that supports a Canadian futures exchange using a Deep SAD-based fraud detection service. Over the last three trading days, investigators have reported a sharp drop in actionable spoofing and layering alerts during the 8:30-10:00 a.m. Montréal time window for front-month TMX equity index futures, even though post-trade reviews still surface suspicious episodes. The issue appeared immediately after a Sunday maintenance release that bundled a score-processing update with alert-package changes. The agenda is to diagnose whether the apparent miss is coming from the detector, score handling, or alert generation path, and to decide what 'stability fix' should be put in place before the next market open. The expected outcome is a concrete overnight action plan, a validation approach for the recent release, and agreement on what will be patched before tomorrow morning.

members.name: Nadia Roy
members.expertise: Exchange surveillance workflows, fraud typologies in futures markets, analyst queue operations, alert tuning in production environments
members.background: Nadia previously worked in compliance operations at a derivatives exchange and now owns product performance for a surveillance platform used by market abuse investigators. She is deeply familiar with spoofing and layering review patterns in limit order book data and tends to evaluate system behavior through what analysts can actually see, triage, and escalate during the trading day.
members.private_state: She wants tomorrow morning's analyst queue to feel normal again without having to publicly admit the Deep SAD rollout created operational risk, and she wants the fix kept narrow enough that it does not disrupt the rest of the client deployment during contract roll.
hidden_assumptions: When people say the system is 'missing fraud,' they mean suspicious episodes fail to appear as investigator-facing alerts in the live queue, not merely that internal anomaly scores changed.

The phrase 'the new logic' refers mainly to the Sunday alert-package update that adjusted morning-session routing and threshold behavior, because that is the visible thing investigators experienced differently.
A 'stability fix' is successful if front-month morning alerts return to roughly last week's practical baseline for analyst review, even if deeper technical cleanup comes later.

Patching 'the morning issue' naturally means a targeted override for the 8:30-10:00 a.m. window on the affected front-month equity index futures book rather than changing the shared pipeline everywhere.
If a suspicious episode was found later in post-trade review, it is fair to call it a known case the live system should have caught.

members.name: Ethan Mercer
members.expertise: Deep anomaly detection, Deep SAD deployment, limit order book feature pipelines, score normalization, production inference diagnostics
members.background: Ethan built much of the firm's Deep SAD training and inference stack for high-frequency futures surveillance. He previously worked on low-latency ML systems for electronic trading infrastructure and is accustomed to reasoning from feature integrity, replay behavior on labeled events, calibration drift, and consistency across shared serving components.
members.private_state: He wants to demonstrate that the core detector is still behaving correctly, avoid a superficial rollback that obscures the actual failure mode, and keep any overnight change technically coherent so it does not introduce cross-contract calibration problems before month-end retraining.
hidden_assumptions: When people say the system 'caught the known cases,' they mean labeled abusive sequences still receive strong anomaly scores in replay or shadow evaluation, regardless of later alert packaging.

The phrase 'the new logic' refers mainly to the score normalization and post-processing path introduced in the Sunday release, because that is the only plausible place where behavior could shift without retraining model weights.

A 'stability fix' is successful if score distributions, replay on labeled fraud windows, and transformation outputs return to expected ranges by tomorrow, even if alert counts are not yet back to last week.
Patching 'the morning issue' means fixing the shared scoring or post-score path whose defect first showed up in the morning session, not applying a one-off local override to a single book.
If labeled replay cases remain separable after the release, the detection layer is functionally intact and the problem lies downstream in thresholding, routing, or case assembly.

misalignment_points.topic: What it means to be missing fraud
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both talk about 'missing fraud,' 'catching the known cases,' and whether the system is still catching abuse.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Nadia means suspicious market episodes that should have surfaced as actionable live alerts to investigators during the morning session.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Ethan means historically labeled abusive event windows still receiving sufficiently extreme anomaly scores in replay or shadow inference, whether or not they became live alerts.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In surveillance teams, people routinely collapse model behavior and investigator outcomes into shorthand like 'catching cases,' so the shared phrase sounds perfectly adequate even though one person is thinking about analyst-visible alerts and the other about detector scoring integrity.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both refer to 'the new logic,' 'the rule update,' or 'what changed Sunday night' as the likely source of the issue.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Nadia is thinking primarily of the alert-package logic changed Sunday night: session-specific routing, threshold packaging, and investigator queue behavior for the morning setup.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Ethan is thinking primarily of the score-processing logic changed in the same release: the score normalizer and post-score transformation path feeding alert generation.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both changes shipped together under one maintenance window and both are plausibly described as 'logic' or a 'rule update,' so the wording feels specific enough in the moment even though each person mentally anchors to a different subsystem.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as stability before tomorrow
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree they need a 'stability fix' and want the system 'stable before tomorrow's open.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Nadia means the 8:30-10:00 a.m. front-month alert flow should look close enough to last week's operational baseline that investigators are no longer missing obvious queue candidates.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Ethan means diagnostic indicators should show the pipeline is technically back in family: expected score distributions, correct replay behavior on labeled fraud windows, and no transformation drift.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are using an urgent operational phrase that sounds shared and goal-oriented, and neither has reason to unpack it because each assumes their own success criterion is the obvious interpretation of 'stable' in a troubleshooting context.

misalignment_points.topic: What it means to patch the morning issue
misalignment_points.surface_form: They discuss 'patching the morning issue' and 'fixing it for the affected book' before the next open.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Nadia assumes this means a narrow operational patch or rollback only for the morning window on the front-month TMX equity index futures book where analysts are currently affected.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Ethan assumes this means implementing a root-cause fix in the shared scoring or post-processing pipeline that will apply consistently across sessions and related contracts, even if the symptom was most visible in that morning book.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The symptom is concentrated in one book and one time window, so talking about 'the morning issue' naturally sounds like shared reference; neither person feels the need to restate boundaries because each assumes the obvious fix scope follows from their own operational frame.
